items: The legal team advised the supplier to comply ____ all updated labeling requirements.
The new policy is intended to protect employees ____ unauthorized disclosure of client data.
The expression 'protect someone from something' takes 'from'.
The sales director attributed the increase in renewals ____ improved follow-up procedures.
The verb 'attribute' takes 'to' before the cause or source.
The branch manager is responsible ____ approving overtime requests during the audit.
The adjective 'responsible' takes 'for' before the duty or task.
The research team is looking forward ____ presenting its findings at the trade show.
The expression 'look forward to' takes 'to' followed by a gerund.
The contractor apologized ____ failing to meet the original installation deadline.
The verb 'apologize' takes 'for' before the reason.
The regional office specializes ____ export documentation for medical equipment.
The verb 'specialize' takes 'in' before a field or area.
The finance committee agreed ____ postpone the vote until the revised figures were available.
The verb 'agree' takes 'to' before an infinitive.
The warranty does not apply ____ damage caused by improper installation.
The expression 'apply to' identifies what a rule or warranty covers.
The consultant warned the client ____ possible delays at the customs checkpoint.
The verb 'warn' takes 'about' before a potential problem.
The customer service team has access ____ the latest troubleshooting database.
The operations chief objected ____ moving the warehouse before peak season ended.
The verb 'object' takes 'to' before a noun or gerund.
The new software is compatible ____ the company's existing accounting system.
The board decided to focus ____ expanding services in smaller cities.
The expression 'focus on' takes 'on' before the area of attention.
The insurer agreed to compensate the retailer ____ losses caused by the storm.
The verb 'compensate' takes 'for' before the loss being covered.
The quality manager insisted ____ inspecting every shipment before release.
The verb 'insist' takes 'on' before a noun or gerund.
The marketing team has been working ____ a campaign aimed at first-time buyers.
The expression 'work on' means to develop or complete something.
The supplier is capable ____ meeting the revised delivery schedule.
The adjective 'capable' takes 'of' before a noun or gerund.
The company is experimenting ____ biodegradable packaging for online orders.
The verb 'experiment' takes 'with' for something being tested.
The new procedure is designed to prevent errors ____ occurring during data entry.
The verb 'prevent' takes 'from' before a gerund.
The manager congratulated the team ____ completing the rollout ahead of schedule.
The verb 'congratulate' takes 'on' before an achievement.
The company has invested heavily ____ cybersecurity training this year.
The technician is familiar ____ the safety procedures for the new equipment.
The committee will vote ____ the proposed changes after hearing from employees.
The verb 'vote' takes 'on' when deciding about a proposal or issue.
The shipment was delayed because the carrier was unable to cope ____ the sudden increase in volume.
The expression 'cope with' means to deal successfully with something difficult.
